issue.title: Reduce the sase.ace import graph: 780 modules and ~0.42s of self-time for one 'import sase.ace.tui.app'
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 1 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

After epic sase-k3 removed persisted diff-badge classification, hidden-row repair, and a double ProjectSpec parse from ACE first paint, Python import is the largest single remaining fixed cost in startup and the one this epic explicitly did not attack.

Measured on athena in workspace sase_11 at master 1f388edee, best of 3 'python -X importtime -c "import sase.ace.tui.app"' runs (host at loadavg ~30/64 cores, so absolute times are inflated):

  modules imported: 2375
  sum of self-times: 1.300 s
  sase.* share: 1661 modules / 0.991 s
  sase.ace.* share: 780 modules / 0.415 s

The same measurement on the pre-epic tree (875f67b74) was 2383 modules / 1.325 s, so phase sase-k3.2's two import-defect fixes removed 8 net modules and a self-time delta inside run-to-run noise. Real-terminal startup telemetry puts process-start-to-on_mount at p50 0.669 s across 9 master sessions, essentially unchanged by the epic.

There is no single slow import: 1,661 sase modules average ~0.6 ms each. The remediation is structural (lazy/deferred imports at the ACE package boundary, splitting eagerly-imported subpackages, or a lazy module proxy), which is why the plan sizes this as an epic with its own design phase rather than a task worker.

Scope requirements from the proposing plan:
- Treat 'python -X importtime' module counts and self-times before/after as the acceptance evidence; do not accept intuition or projections.
- Pair it with a real-terminal capture of process_start_to_on_mount_seconds from ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl (see docs/perf_runbook.md, 'Startup telemetry capture') so the import win is confirmed end to end and not just in a synthetic import.
- Keep the subprocess import-graph guard tests added by sase-k3.2 (tests/ace/tui/test_lazy_imports.py) as the pattern for locking in each removal.

The right next step is /sase_plan, not a direct implementation.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-fy — closed as canceled on 2026-08-06; it proposed breaking the single 497-module src/sase import cycle to make static test selection precise. Different motivation (selection precision, not ACE startup) and different remediation, but the same package-layout surface: a plan for this task should decide whether breaking that cycle is a prerequisite, a subsumed deliverable, or out of scope. sase-fy's triage note explicitly says the right next step for it is /sase_plan.
